name: Athaliah
source_summary: Ahab and Jezebel's daughter, who married into Judah's royal line, seized the throne by massacring her own grandchildren after her son's death, reigned six years, and was overthrown and executed by Jehoiada the priest.
family_friendly_summary: Athaliah was the daughter of the wicked King Ahab and Queen Jezebel of Israel, and she married into the royal family of Judah. When her son, King Ahaziah, was killed, Athaliah did something shocking: she tried to have all of her own grandchildren, the rest of the royal family, killed so that she alone could rule as queen. But one baby grandson, Joash, was secretly rescued and hidden away by his aunt for six years. When Joash was seven, the priest Jehoiada organized a plan to reveal him publicly and crown him as the rightful king, and Athaliah was overthrown and put to death. Her reign is remembered as one of the darkest chapters in Judah's history, both for how she seized power and for the idol worship she encouraged.
adult_story: Athaliah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, married Jehoram of Judah, bringing Israel's Baal worship into the southern kingdom's royal family (2 Kings 8:18, 26-27; 2 Chronicles 21:6). When her son Ahaziah was killed by Jehu during his purge of Ahab's dynasty, Athaliah seized the opportunity with shocking ruthlessness: she "destroyed all the royal offspring" of Judah, her own grandchildren, to eliminate any rival claim and rule Judah outright herself (2 Kings 11:1). One infant grandson, Joash, was secretly rescued by his aunt Jehosheba, wife of the priest Jehoiada, and hidden in the temple for six years while Athaliah reigned over the land (11:2-3). In the seventh year, Jehoiada organized a coordinated, carefully guarded coronation, presenting seven-year-old Joash publicly as the rightful Davidic king; when Athaliah heard the crowd's rejoicing and rushed in, tearing her clothes and crying "treason, treason," Jehoiada ordered her removed from the temple and executed outside its gates so no blood would be shed in the LORD's house (11:4-16). Her death ended the only interruption of the Davidic line's continuous rule over Judah in the entire Old Testament, and the temple of Baal she had promoted in Jerusalem was torn down immediately afterward, its altars smashed and its priest killed (11:17-18) -- a violent close to a reign built on the murder of her own family.
devotionals: Athaliah’s story teaches us about usurpation; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Athaliah’s experience of idolatry, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
